column4: cleat#3171: this registeredBackends test calls backend.Setup(t) separately inside each of its three settlement-case subtests (resolve/reject/createUpdateRequest) rather than once per dialect, so a non-exercised dialect skips three times, not one. This job supplies MySQL only, so the Postgres and SQL Server arms each skip all three cases -- six, not two. Measured by NAME with only CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL set: go test ./engine/ -run TestAPromiseOrUpdateSettledWhileTheWorkflowIsAwakeStillWakesIt -count=1 -json reports exactly these six skip events and three passes (the MySQL arm).

cleat#3171: same test as the line above, mirrored -- this job supplies SQL Server only, so the Postgres and MySQL arms each skip all three cases. Measured by NAME with only CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL set: six skip events, three passes (the SQL Server arm).

cleat#3171: this job (go test ./engine/... with only CLEAT_TEST_DB set) runs Postgres and skips MySQL and SQL Server. Per-SETTLEMENT-CASE, not per-dialect, because backend.Setup(t) is called inside each case's own t.Run rather than once before the case loop -- six skips, not two. Measured on this PR's own cluster job: the skip-budget guard reported 621 actual skips against a 615 inherited allowance, a difference of exactly 6.

Pairing line for the cluster entry above, required by scripts/check-skip-ledger-engine-coverage.py: engine-race.yml runs with the same single-DSN (postgres-only) shape as the cluster job, so the same six subtests skip there too. Identical regex to the cluster line, as the pairing check requires; not independently measured against a live engine-race.yml run (it is not a per-PR job), but the dialect gating is the same mechanism as the cluster line, which was measured.
